About this document


This document provides the teaching content for Resistant Materials Technology
Years 11–13 of the New Zealand Curriculum.

Progress and assessment information for Resistant Materials Technology Years 11–
13 is still in development. Once that is completed, Resistant Materials Technology
Years 11–13 is proposed to be made by the Minister of Education as a National
Curriculum Statement under section 90(1)(a) of the Education and Training Act 2020.

It is proposed that, once made and published in the New Zealand Gazette, schools
who offer Resistant Materials Technology Years 11–13 will be required to start using
it in Year 11 from 1 January 2028, in Year 12 from 1 January 2029, and in Year 13
from 1 January 2030.

This document will be replaced with the official version made under the Act and
published in the New Zealand Gazette once that has occurred.

  consider the end users and the intended environments for the outcomes, through
  creative problem-solving, technological practice, and innovation. Resistant
  materials which can be categorised as traditional, composite or emerging, will be
  considered for selection by the students for use in the tangible outcomes,
  informed by what they have been taught in terms of materials heritage,

Through the study of Resistant Materials Technology students are taught to apply
knowledge of materials, manufacturing processes, and engineering principles to
design and construct functional products that meet identified needs and
specifications. They are taught how material properties, technological developments,
user requirements, environmental considerations, and production processes influence
design decisions, product performance, and the development of engineered
outcomes.
Resistant Materials Technology provides students with the knowledge and practices
to investigate, design, represent, evaluate, and manufacture products using a range
of materials, techniques, and technologies. This disciplinary knowledge equips
students to make informed decisions by balancing functionality, efficiency,
sustainability, quality, and fitness for purpose.
As students progress through Years 11–13, they are taught to select and apply
appropriate materials and manufacturing methods, communicate ideas through
written, technical, and digital representations, and manage increasingly complex
design and production processes. They make increasingly sophisticated decisions
about design and manufacturing by considering the environmental, social, and
cultural perspectives that influence material selection, design decisions, and
manufacturing processes.

 Disciplinary writing

 Focus: the use of writing to reflect the ways in which knowledge is organised, analysed, and communicated within Resistant Materials Technology
 In Resistant Materials Technology, writing is an analytical and reflective practice that enables students to develop and refine ideas through description, explanation, and
 evaluation of products and production processes, while communicating informed understandings of their own and others’ work.

In Year 13, students are taught using contexts that require informed decision-making
to address complex design and manufacturing challenges through the integration of
materials, technologies, processes, and systems. Complexity arises from the
sophistication of the design problem and the interaction of multiple requirements
rather than the size of the outcome.
